title: The rendered prompts: what to do about size and example names

sections.title: Rendering the real prompts
sections.intro: `npm run prompt:render` planned hub/chat (tools mode, GPT-6 Luna) and hub/chat_small (static mode, a 2k-window qwen2.5:3b) for "I keep forgetting what I spend on groceries" on a fresh hub with every system, without calling a model. No known fn is spelled `system/name` anywhere. Three things need a call; the files are in the review next to this set.

questions.question: Made-up example fn names in descriptions (e.g. `database/main.overdue_invoices`, `input/trip_details`, ×20+) still reach the model in slash form, because the registry can't know a fn that doesn't exist. What should happen?
questions.why: It breaks "the slash form is invisible to the model" in the very places the model learns what a name looks like.

options.label: Encode by rule
options.description: `text()` also converts any token shaped like a fn name (`<known system>/<name>`, with dots) to the `__` form even when no such fn exists, except known context keys and kinds (`database/guide`, `database/query`). The format is computable from the name; only reading cut names back needs the registry.

options.label: Authors mark examples
options.description: Example names are written `fn:database/main.overdue_invoices`; the build warns on unmarked ones. Explicit, but every system author must remember.

options.label: Rewrite the examples in model form
options.description: Write `database__main__overdue_invoices` directly in the descriptions. Breaks the rule that authors write qualified names.

questions.question: hub/chat_small doesn't fit a 2,048-token window: the `<systems>` list alone is ~2,560 tokens (each system's long `about`), the static tools ~1,600, against 1,413 of room. What should small agents get?
questions.why: Static + graph mode exists for small local models; today it can't take a single message at 2k.

options.label: The systems list follows the agent's detail
options.description: At `injected.detail: 'summary'` each system is one line (name + its short description), not its `about`; static tool descriptions get a short form too (their examples stay). Add a test that hub/chat_small's fixed part fits a 2k model with room for a message.

options.label: No systems list for small agents
options.description: They find systems through `find`; smallest, but the model can't answer "what can you do" without searching.

options.label: Accept a bigger minimum window
options.description: Declare chat_small for 4k+ windows (qwen2.5:3b can run at 4k–8k num_ctx) and leave the text as is.

questions.question: hub/chat's first user message is 5,344 tokens: the no-model suggestions arrive as full fn cards with their whole return types (`database__get_query`'s alone is huge). How big should a suggestion be?
questions.why: Every message pays this; suggestions are hints, and the model loads what it uses (which brings the full schema as a tool).

options.label: Brief cards
options.description: A suggested fn is its name, label, description and first example args; the full args/returns come when it's loaded (or with `inspect`). Context suggestions: title + summary.

options.label: Full cards, under a token cap
options.description: Keep full cards but cap the suggestions block (e.g. 1,500 tokens) and drop the lowest scores.

options.label: Keep as is
options.description: Full cards; the model sees everything up front.
